subject: Patient:0c04d9fb-d8d0-4ee0-8fc9-0c3f7f148bdf
evidence:
Tissue Removed
Damaged cartilage and subchondral bone from the left acetabulum and femoral head

Prostheses or Implants
Cemented total hip prosthesis consisting of a polyethylene acetabular component and a metal femoral component

Estimated Blood Loss
300ml

Complications
None noted

Post-Operative Care
- Prophylactic anticoagulation with enoxaparin 40mg SC injection once daily for 28 days
- Regular oral paracetamol 1g QDS
- Oral tramadol 50mg 6-hourly PRN for breakthrough pain
- IV cefuroxime 1.5g pozt-operatively for 24 hours to minimise infection risk

Plan
- Encourage early mobilisation with physiotherapy
- Monitor surgical site for signs of infection or haematoma
- Ensure adequate hydration and nutritional support

- Endo: No polyuria, polydipsia, or heat/cold intolerance
- Other: No recent fever or weight changes

Past Medical History
- HTN
- Mild osteoarthritis

Medications
- No regular medications
- IV paracetamol 1g QID prescribed during ED stay to manage pain and prevent discomfort

Allergies
None

Social History
- Lives alone in a ground-floor flat
- Independent with activities of daily living
- Retired accountant
- Non-smoker
- Drinks alcohol occasionally, approximately 6 units per week
- No recreational drug use

Family History
- Father: Deceased, history of MI at age 67
- Motherr: Deceased, history of HTN and stroke
- No known family history of neurodegenerative or psychiatric disorders

On Examination
- Alert but mildly confused, GCS 14/15 (disoriented to time)
- Appears dehydrated with dry mucous membranes
- No obvious signs of head trauma or external injuries
- Neurological examination:
   - Cranial nerves: Intact, pupils equal and reactive to light bilaterally
  - Motor: Normal power (5/5) in all limbs
  - Sensory: No deficits detected in light touch, pinprick, or vibratkion sensation
  - Reflexes: Normal and symmetrical in all limbs, plantar reflexes downgoing bilaterally
 - Coordination: No dysmetria or intention tremor on finger-nose testing

- Respiratory: Equal air entry bilaterally, no added sounds

- No meningeal signs

HR 88
BP 142/86
RR 16

SpO2 98% on room air

- CT head (02/01/26): DSubdural hygroma noted, no MLS

- CRP: Normal
- LFTs: Normal
- Coagulation profile: Normal
- Blood glucose: Normal
- Pending: None

Minimal

- Encourage mobilisation with physiotherapy as per post-op protocol
- Continue routine post-op care and pain management as required

subject: Patient:420df33b-0072-4124-b1c6-0589daef3677
evidence:
Mabel Grace Turner

Anaesthesia Type
Spinal anaesthesia with sedation

Procedure
Total left hip replacement

Incision
Posterolateral approach to the left hip

Diagnosis
End-stage OA of the left hip

Findings
- Advanced degeneration of the left hip joint with severe cartilage erosion
- No evidence of surrounding tissue infection or abnormal pathology

Tissue Removed
Degenerated left femoral head and acetabular cartilage

Prostheses or Implants
- Cemented femoral stem prosthesis
- Cemented acetabular cup prosthesis

Closure Technique
- Wound closed in layers using absorbable sutures for deep layers
- Skin closed with absorbable sutures
- Sterile dressing applied over the surgical site

Estimated Blood Loss
300 mL

Complications
None noted

Post-Operative Care
- Initiate enoxaparin 40 mg SC once daily for VTE prophylaxis
- Paracetamol 1 g every 6 hrs for pain control
- Tramadol 50 mg PRN for breakthrough pain
- Monitor surgical site for signs of infection or wound complications
- Antibiotics ont prescribed due to the patientâ€™s penicillin allergy

Plan
- Encourage early mobilisation with physio starting on postop day 1
- Regular assessment of pain control and functional progress
- Schedule follow-up in ortho outpatient clinic in six weeks
- Send tissue specimens to histology for further analysis

- Underlying subchondral bone from the left femoral head adn acetabulum

- Cementless acetabular c omponent
- Cementless femoral stem with modular head

- Deep layers closed with absorbable sutures

- Sterile ddressing applied over the incision

300 mL

None encountered

- Prescribe Cefuroxime 1.5 g IV every 8 hours for 24 hours for infection prophylaxis
- Start enoxaparin 40 mg SC once daily for thromboprophylaxs
- Regular p aracetamol 1 g every 6 hours and ibuprofen 400 mg every 8 hours for post-op pain management
- Prescribe morphine 10 mg PRN for breakthrough pain
- Schedule initial physio session the following morning

Plan
- Encourage mobilisation as per physio guidance starting on 04/01/26

subject: Patient:f44d4a08-4c76-4000-ad61-d1d81032e643
evidence:
Ethel Joanne Duffy

Anaesthesia Type
GA

Procedure
Total left hip replacement

Incision
Posterolateral approach to the left hip

Diagnosis
End-stag OA of the left hip

Findings
- Severe cartilage degeneration noted in the acetabulum and femoral head
- Surrounding soft tissues appeared unremarkable with no evidece of acute inflammation or infection

Tissue Removed
- Degenerated femoral head of the left hip
- Damaged cartilage from the acetabular surface

Prostheses or Implants
- Cemented acetabular cup
- Cemented femoral stem with amodular head

Closure Technique
- Layers closed using absorbable wsutures for deep tissue
- Skin closed with staples
- Sterile dressing applied

Estimated Blood Loss
250 mL

Complications
None

Post-Operative Care
- Prophylactic enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously once daily for 4 weeks to reduce risk of DVT
- Oral oxycodone 5 mg every 4â€“6 hours as needed for pain control
- No further doses of IV cefuroxime required after intraoperative admiinistration

Plan
- Encourage mobilisation with physio startnig on postoperative day 1
- Monitor for signs of infection or thromboembolic events
- Reassess pain management requirements daily
- Send removed tissue (degenerative femoral head and damaged cartilage) for histopathology

Additional Notes
- Consultant oversight provided by Dr.
